title: routing-governance-and-adapter-roster
content:
Purpose:
This working note captures a pragmatic ownership and routing governance proposal for the control plane surface that sits above the serving runtime. Focus areas: API gateway responsibilities, the orchestration layer's job boundaries, runtime adapter responsibilities, and multi-region routing/failover rules.

Status and intent:
- Draft for platform-engineering review.
- Goal: reduce ambiguity in on-call, deployment, and feature rollout ownership while enabling region-aware routing and graceful degradation.
- This is deliberately operational: includes examples, handoff rules, and short checklists for launches.

High-level summary:
- API Gateway = north-south entry point. Responsibilities: auth/quotas/rate-limit/blocking, coarse routing (region preference, tiering), request validation and enrichment, and returning standardized error taxonomy to clients. Not responsible for per-model fallback logic beyond header-based routing hints.
- Orchestration plane = policy decision and routing orchestration. Responsibilities: per-customer routing policies (which region/model variant), rollout/A/B policies, failure domain awareness, and conversion of high-level decisions into adapter calls. Not responsible for heavy traffic shaping or per-token optimizations.
- Runtime adapters = southbound adapters that translate orchestration decisions into concrete runtime actions (launch/scale model instances, select quantized binary, bind KV caches). Responsibilities: model variant compatibility, health signaling, capacity accounting. Not responsible for policy decisions or auth.

Ownership matrix (proposed):
- API Gateway: eng-platform-api (owner on call, SLAs for 5xx and auth errors).
- Orchestration: eng-platform-orchestration (owner for routing policy UI/CLI, rollout logic).
- Runtime adapters: eng-serving-runtime (owner for adapters per cloud/hardware, adapter contract stability).
- Observability & tracing plumbing: shared responsibility between eng-platform-observability and the owning service for instrumentation scope.

Routing policy primitives (for policy authors):
- region_preference: ordered list of regions (e.g., [us-east1, us-west1, eu-west1]).
- tier_priority: e.g., [dedicated, hosted, private-fallback].
- max_latency_ms: soft target; orchestration uses historical p95 to decide.
- degrade_grace: how long to allow stale KV cache hits before rejecting.
- model_family_fallbacks: mapping from family->fallback-variants.

Example routing flows (common cases):
1) Normal request: client -> API gateway (auth, quota) -> orchestration (checks region_preference, tenant pinned model) -> runtime adapter in preferred region -> runtime.
2) Preferred region saturated: orchestration checks tier_priority, routes to next candidate; if model variants incompatible, orchestration triggers adapter to select compatible quantized variant and annotates response with warning header.
3) Regional outage: API gateway will accept requests from clients globally but orchestration will apply emergency routing policy (e.g., route to backup-exclusive region or degrade to lower-capacity tier).

Adapter contract (minimum surface):
- Health endpoint: /adapter/health (ok | degraded | critical) with short JSON (version, model-list, capacity_estimate).
- Capability descriptor: returns supported model families, quantization profiles, max_seq_len, per-request latency estimate for typical batch sizes.
- Bind call: API to attach a model variant to a runtime pool with config knobs (batch_size_hint, kv_cache_enabled).
- Metrics: adapters must export per-variant token-rate, error-rate, and avg-latency with agreed metric names.

Multi-region and failover rules (operator playbook):
- Precondition: each customer has a primary region and zero+ failover regions declared in the account profile.
- Failover threshold: if p95 latency > X ms or error-rate > Y over 5m, orchestration flags region degraded.
- Blackout vs degraded: blackouts (total unreachable) trigger immediate failover; degraded allows for scaled-down traffic with explicit warn header.
- Data residency: for customers with residency requirements, orchestration will never route outside allowed regions even during outages (must escalate to SRE).

Deployment & rollout responsibilities:
- Feature behind rollout flag: orchestration team owns flags and rollout UI; adapters must be backward compatible for 90 days with previous adapter API.
- Canarying: A/B and canary deployments defined as orchestration-level rollout policies; orchestration should only direct a small percentage to new adapters/regions until runtime adapters emit stability metrics for 24h.
- Schema changes: if adapter contract changes, adapters must publish migration notes and support old contract for 2 weeks or until all regions upgraded.

Operational runbooks (brief):
- API Gateway 5xx spike: oncall checks auth subsystem, token-signing KMS, and rate-limiter backpressure; if upstream (orchestration) is impacted, mark downstream degraded.
- Orchestration stuck in pending: check policy-store (consistency across replicas), then adapter control plane connectivity.
- Adapter degraded: if capacity_estimate drops below threshold, orchestration should be able to re-route. If not, emergency escalation to eng-serving-runtime.

Open questions / decision points:
- Should the API Gateway perform any automatic per-request region affinity (sticky routing) or leave affinity to orchestration? Proposal: keep affinity in orchestration to centralize policy and make gateway simpler.
- How strict should adapter contract be on metrics naming and cardinality? Need a short spec.
- Cross-tenant batching: where is the policy boundary? Orchestration should own batching policies but adapters implement them — need interface for batching hints.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- Review: eng-platform-api, eng-platform-orchestration, eng-serving-runtime to sign off on ownership lines (Priya to coordinate).
- Draft adapter-metrics-spec PR: Miguel to author.
- Small PoC: implement orchestration region_preference switch for one internal test-tenant and exercise failover path (Ethan + Sofia).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light on implementation detail and heavy on operational responsibilities; once owners agree on boundaries we will convert to a sequence diagram and an ownership SLAs table.
- Prefer to keep adapters dumb about policy decisions — they should expose capabilities and accept commands.

References and useful tickets:
- PL-789: multi-region policy store work (linked above).
- PR: control-plane/orchestration#412 — early routing policy implementation.

End of note.
